specific_confirmatory_diagnostic_tests.textbook_diagnostic_criteria_summary: Plasma cortisol is measured before, 4-, and 8-hours after IV administration of 0.01 mg/kg dexamethasone. Cortisol above laboratory cut-off (1 or 1.4 mcg/dL) at 8-hours post-dexamethasone confirms hypercortisolism. Suppression of >50% from basal at 4 or 8-hours is compatible with PDH.

Integrated measure of corticoid production performed on 2 consecutive morning urine samples collected at home. Useful combined with oral HDDST to diagnose and discriminate pituitary from adrenal sources.

Plasma cortisol is measured before and 1 hour after administration of synthetic ACTH (5 mcg/kg IV or IM). Screens for hypercortisolism based on excessive cortisol response but does not differentiate pituitary from adrenal dependent disease.

Most accurate stand-alone biochemical test for discriminating pituitary from adrenal origin in dogs with proven hypercortisolism. Low or undetectable concentrations are expected in adrenal-dependent cases. Strict handling requires chilled tubes and immediate freezing.

Used to help differentiate pituitary from adrenal hypercortisolism when LDDST demonstrates no suppression. Given as 0.1 mg/kg IV dexamethasone. >50% suppression indicates pituitary origin, but it provides differentiation in only 12% additional dogs over LDDST and is generally no longer recommended over imaging.

specific_confirmatory_diagnostic_tests.textbook_diagnostic_criteria_summary: Gold standard test. Serum cortisol concentrations before and 1 hour after IV administration of 1 mcg/kg synthetic short-acting ACTH are <1 mcg/dL (<28 nmol/L).
Screening assay. Basal serum cortisol concentration >2 mcg/dL (>55 nmol/L) makes HA unlikely, effectively excluding the diagnosis. Concentrations <2 mcg/dL require an ACTHst for confirmation.

specific_confirmatory_diagnostic_tests.textbook_diagnostic_criteria_summary: Uterine horns distended with intraluminal fluid, with or without flocculation. Uterine wall thickened with irregular edges and small hypoechoic areas consistent with cystic change (CEH).
Allows determination of site of origin of purulent vulvar discharge in dogs with no apparent uterine enlargement; not possible in cats.

specific_confirmatory_diagnostic_tests.textbook_diagnostic_criteria_summary: Pyloric malposition with gastric air entrapment ('Popeye arm', 'double bubble'). Shows the classic compartmentalization of the stomach, which is pathognomonic. May also show gas bubbles within the gastric wall indicating necrosis, or pneumoperitoneum.

Helpful to confirm diagnosis in subsets of patients with organoaxial volvulus (normal positioned stomach with gastric dilatation). Can also identify abdominal effusion or air from hemoabdomen or perforation.
